config.title: Context Performance

intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Angular application that demonstrates how to optimize performance using context. You'll learn how to use Angular's change detection strategies and context providers to prevent unnecessary re-renders of components. The core concept involves understanding how data flows through your application and controlling when components update. You'll work with Angular's built-in performance features like ChangeDetectionStrategy and context providers to make your app faster and more efficient.
intro.usecase: In enterprise applications like financial dashboards or e-commerce admin panels, you often need to share data across multiple components without prop drilling. For example, a dashboard might have a theme switcher that affects dozens of child components, or a product filter that needs to update various display panels. Using context effectively prevents unnecessary re-renders when only specific parts of the UI depend on changed data. This pattern is crucial for maintaining performance in complex interfaces where data flows through many nested components.

objectives: Implement a context service to manage shared state across components
Configure dependency injection to provide context at the appropriate module level
Apply change detection strategies to optimize context updates
Construct observable data streams for reactive context consumption
Bind context values to template expressions using the async pipe
Control context subscription lifecycle to prevent memory leaks
Integrate context with Angular's built-in performance features

steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add two public properties: renderCount of type number initialized to 0, and lastRenderTime of type number initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body, using TypeScript type annotations and initial values.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.hint: Implement ngDoCheck() to track how often change detection runs. Inside it, increment renderCount and update lastRenderTime with the current timestamp.
